author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this talk, he will share the CORE System—a clear, actionable approach to building discipline that lasts. Rather than cold showers or endless hours of grind, he shows how structure, alignment, and small consistent steps can turn chaos into clarity and create habits that stick—discipline anyone can learn and use to build a meaningful, fulfilling life. 

Angelo Rachou, a French student studying industrial engineering and a passionate content creator. Coming from a scientific and engineering background, he has been trained to see the world as systems, processes, and repeatable patterns. During his year abroad, he combined this mindset with his experience as a top student and creator to reverse-engineer a practical framework for discipline. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How to build discipline without punishing yourself | Angelo Rachou | TEDxEHLLausanne

Dr. Manesh Agarwal is a healthcare leader with over 25 years of experience across diverse medical systems and institutions in seven cities. Guided by service, lifelong learning, and the influence of mentors and family, he brings a deeply human perspective to leadership, growth, and transformation in healthcare. author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the health of our cities could be measured by the songs of birds?

In this powerful, visually striking TEDx talk, Dr. Bushra Nisar Khan takes on the journey from corridors of Lahore Zoo to diverse campuses of University of the Punjab. 

She reveals how the birds are planet's "living alarm system" and why their disappearance is a warning sign of hidden health crisis. Discover the science behind our daily waste and how can we restore balance to our environment.  Dr. Bushra Nisar Khan is an academic and researcher in zoology, known for her work in biodiversity and ecological documentation. Her recent research documenting bird species at Punjab University reflects a commitment to environmental conservation and to using academic work to raise awareness of local ecosystems and natural heritage. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: When Birds Speak The Nature Whisper | Dr. Bushra Nisar Khan | TEDxPunjab University

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The Bhulan is blind, yet it navigates the Indus with more instinct than we do. In this powerful talk, Hamera Aisha explores the bond between the Indus River, its people and the endangered dolphins we cannot afford to lose. 

She shares how blind dolphins teach us about resilience. Hamera Aisha is a wildlife conservationist working with WWF Pakistan, contributing to initiatives focused on biodiversity protection and environmental sustainability. Her work highlights the importance of conservation at both community and policy levels, reflecting a growing need to protect natural ecosystems through awareness, research, and collective action. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Resilience From The Indus River | Hamera Aisha | TEDxPunjab University

As artificial intelligence and modern convenience increasingly remove discomfort from daily life, what happens to the human experience of growth? In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Kevin Williams explores the relationship between struggle, resilience, and meaning in an AI-driven world. Challenging the pursuit of constant ease and optimization, he argues that some of the most important parts of being human are forged through adversity, effort, and challenge. Vistage Chair and tech leader; founder of Drawbridge Solutions and
owner of Escapology Columbia. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description:
Pervaiz Hoodbhoy renowned physicist and public intellectual Pervez Hoodbhoy delivered a talk titled “Education in Crisis: Why Reforming Minds Matters More Than Rewriting Curricula.”

In his thought-provoking address, he challenged the common belief that educational change was only about updating textbooks. Instead, he highlighted a deeper crisis the urgent need to transform how we think, question, and learn.

The talk served as a powerful call to move beyond surface-level reforms and focus on shaping critical, curious, and independent minds for the future. Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy is a Pakistani nuclear physicist and author. He has been considered by many as one of the most vocal, progressive and liberal member of the Pakistani intelligentsia.Hoodbhoy is known for his opposition to nuclear weapons and vocal defence of secularism, freedom of speech, scientific temper and education in Pakistan This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized
title: Education in Crisis | Pervaiz Hoodbhoy | TEDxRMI

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Mr & Mrs Uzair shared powerful insights in their talk titled “On Belay: Rising Through Fear, Failure, and the Thin Air of Possibility.”

They spoke about how fear, failure, and uncertainty are inevitable parts of every journey, but they do not define who we are. Through their discussion, they highlighted that true growth comes from facing challenges head-on, embracing discomfort, and learning from setbacks.

Their talk inspired the audience to see fear not as a barrier, but as a starting point for growth and to dare to explore new possibilities that lead to greater personal and professional heights. Lahore-based Ahmed Uzair and Anum Uzair have become the first Pakistani couple to summit the world’s eighth-highest peak Mt Manaslu 8,163 metres tall  in Nepal. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: On Belay: Rising through fear , failure and thin air of possibility | Anum Uzair | TEDxRMI

In her TEDx talk, Adele invites audiences to rethink everything they’ve been taught about work. Through honest reflection and real-world insight, she challenges us to break free from rigid career paths and instead design lives that allow us to create, work, and truly live on our own terms.
 Adele Tilley-Jones is a Senior Lecturer & Programme Leader in Entrepreneurship within the Faculty of Business and Law. An experienced business director whose career has been shaped not by a straight line, but by courage, change, and lived experience. title: The future of work: Reimagining the 9 to 5. | Adele Tilly-Jones | TEDxDeMontfortU

description: AI is transforming how we work and learn — but our most powerful technology is still the human mind. This talk explores how adaptability, empathy, and collaboration will define success in the age of artificial intelligence. Drawing on a journey from lawyer to academic leader and England dodgeball player, Brett shows how the same qualities that drive high-performing teams; resilience, communication, and trust can help us navigate an unpredictable, AI-driven world. “The Human Edge” challenges us to see technology not as competition, but as a catalyst for reimagining what it means to be human at work. Brett Koenig is the Associate Head of Law at De Montfort University, where he leads innovation in AI and education. Before entering academia, Brett practised as a lawyer and also represented England internationally in dodgeball, serving as the current captain. title: Thriving in an age of artificial intelligence | Brett Koenig | TEDxDeMontfortU

author: TEDx Talks
description: The future of office work is at a critical junction. Post-pandemic, the tide is turning on the work from home generation and employees are returning to a more formally structured working week. The direction that the landscape of work takes over the next few years will shape so many other aspects of our lives – our wellbeing, work-life-balance, the daily rhythms of our families, where we choose to live, how we travel. My research brings together the lessons from the past and the lens of popular culture in the present to rethink the future space that work might inhabit. Nicola Bishop is an education developer, popular culture researcher, and self-confessed 90s sitcom superfan. Her research examines how office work has been represented in literature, television, and film since the 1850s. Her book Lower-Middle-Class Nation explores the cultural history of the white-collar office worker and how perceptions of office life shape attitudes towards modern living. title: How popular culture will shape the future of office work | Nicola Bishop | TEDxDeMontfortU

description: Creativity should be equal to literacy and numeracy in all walks of life. Chris Wright is a practicing artist and designer alongside this he has 30 years of experience in education. With a passion to promote creativity in all forms of experiential learning and play. His work focuses on promoting innovative approaches to teaching and learning. Chris has contributed to discussions on creative education through interviews with multiple publications, a radio feature for the Learning and Teaching Festival on Radio Leicester, and presentations at teaching and learning conferences. Most recently, he appeared on a Times Higher Education podcast discussing mental wellbeing and creativity in education.
